item.title: Kolkata: Video shows crowd breaching barricades, tussling with cops day before stampede
item.description: A crowd surge at Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata led to a tragic stampede on Saturday evening. The incident occurred when heavy rain caused a rush of people seeking shelter inside the pandal. Eyewitnesses described a chaotic scene with limited crowd management and dark conditions. Following the tragedy, investigations are underway and several organisers have been detained for questioning.
item.dc:creator: SHREEDHAR RATHI

item.title: ‘Unfair’ treatment of Kuldeep Yadav? Ashwin fears another benching on NZ tour
item.description: Ravichandran Ashwin voices his disappointment over Kuldeep Yadav's exclusion from the Indian cricket team, arguing that a single bowler shouldn't bear the brunt of criticism when conditions are tough. He predicts that Varun Chakravarthy may be favored for the New Zealand series instead of Kuldeep. Ashwin raises concerns about India prioritizing batting strength over specialized bowlers, stressing the importance of having real wicket-takers if four seamers are in play.
item.dc:creator: DIPTAYAN HAZRA

item.title: ‘Crocodiles will eat her’: How a shopping promise led to nursing officer’s murder
item.description: A nursing officer named Snehlata went missing after her partner, Satyaprakash, took her out under false premises. Police suspect he murdered her due to conflicts regarding their child and their relationship dynamics. Satyaprakash allegedly confessed to strangling her and disposing of her body into the Pachnada river. Her family is demanding action against him as the search for her remains continues.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Shark Tank’s Kevin O’Leary: Engineering is no longer the only education worth getting
item.description: Canadian billionaire and Shark Tank judge Kevin O’Leary has said he no longer believes engineering is the only education worth pursuing. In a post on X, O’Leary argued that storytelling, photography, video editing and content creation have become highly lucrative skills, with creators earning from contracts with multiple companies by helping brands lower customer acquisition costs and improve returns on advertising spend.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Besieged cities, broken supply routes: Can Yemen hold its ground against Houthis
item.description: Yemen’s government forces face mounting difficulties as they strive to sustain their offensive against Houthi rebels. Supply routes have been severely disrupted, leading to territorial setbacks and soaring fuel costs in areas they control. The fall of key locations like the Red Sea port of Mocha only complicates matters further. Additionally, internal rifts among competing factions hinder operational efficiency, while Saudi military assistance remains vital for campaign success.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Man skipped ITR, declared Rs 12.9L income after notice; ITAT cancels 200% penalty
item.description: The man in this case failed to file his income tax return, and the Income Tax Department issued him a notice. He subsequently responded by filing an ITR for assessment year (AY) 2018-19, reporting an income of Rs 12.9 lakh. However, the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) took the view that this income would have remained outside the tax net had the department not issued the notice to the man.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: Kolkata stampede: SIT to probe security lapses after 19 deaths; 7 arrested
item.description: A tragic stampede occurred at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal, resulting in 19 fatalities and multiple injuries. The West Bengal government announced the formation of a special investigation team to look into the incident. Overcrowding and rain exacerbated the chaos, affecting visitor safety at the pandal. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari confirmed that puja committee members were detained for questioning regarding security arrangements.
item.dc:creator: SHREEDHAR RATHI

item.title: ‘I will retire’: Medvedev threatens umpire in dramatic Shanghai loss - Watch
item.description: Daniil Medvedev threatened to retire from his Shanghai Masters semi-final against Rafael Jodar after officials refused to replay the Spaniard’s previous shot. The umpire eventually agreed to show it, prompting commentators to question Medvedev’s intentions. Some suspected he was buying recovery time. Despite the heated argument, Jodar defeated Medvedev 6-3, 6-4 to reach the final.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: California farm makes 10x more leasing land for solar than wheat
item.description: In Tulare County, California, the Changala family farm has embraced a transformative shift from dry-farmed wheat to solar energy. Driven by financial incentives, solar leases are now yielding significantly greater income compared to traditional crops. Facing water scarcity in the San Joaquin Valley, farmers are increasingly investing in solar technologies.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Oregon woman sold home to son-in-law for $270,000; court rejects right to stay
item.description: An Oregon woman who sold her home worth approximately $398,000 to her son-in-law for $270,000 in 2006 claimed she was promised the right to live there for life. After a dispute over her occupancy, a trial court ruled in her favour. However, the Oregon Court of Appeals overturned the decision, finding that the written sale documents transferred her entire ownership interest without reserving a life estate.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Jack Dorsey’s $32M mansion renovation continues after 14 years; neighbors fed up
item.description: Since acquiring his opulent mansion in San Francisco for $9.99 million back in 2012, Jack Dorsey has been immersed in a major renovation project. The reconstruction has caused disruptions and complaints from nearby residents due to the ongoing noise. Enhancements include seismic upgrades, solar panels, and landscaped roofs. Dorsey also extended his property portfolio in 2018 with a $21.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Why kids act different around cousins than classmates, per psychology
item.description: When children interact with their cousins, their behavior often contrasts sharply with how they act around classmates. The comfort of family ties leads to playful banter among cousins but might trigger shyness in structured school environments. Families can inadvertently stoke competition during gatherings, making comparisons inevitable. For parents, recognizing these variations is essential to nurture healthy social growth in children.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Yet another infra scare, 12-tonne steel cage crashes onto moving car in Mumbai
item.description: On Saturday afternoon, a steel reinforcement cage fell on a moving sedan on the Eastern Express Highway. Eyewitnesses reported a loud creaking noise preceding the incident, which caused structural damage to the vehicle. Fortunately, the driver and passengers escaped with minor injuries, but no serious harm was reported. The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority imposed a penalty on the contractor and initiated an investigation after the collapse.
item.dc:creator: MANOJ BADGERI

item.title: You earn, save & invest. Does that mean you're financially literate?
item.description: Financial literacy encompasses understanding one's income, expenses, and the risks associated with investments. Differentiating between saving and investing is crucial for effective financial planning. Individuals must be vigilant against financial fraud and misleading guidance in their investment choices. A well-structured financial plan aids in aligning savings and investments with personal objectives. Familiarity with financial concepts empowers individuals to make thoughtful decisions and manage their finances responsibly.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: Chethan Kumar in Parallax: Made in India isn’t enough. It has to be made by India
item.description: India is called to transition from simply assembling products to developing and owning its technologies. This pivotal shift aims to establish a robust intellectual property framework that fosters local talent. Focusing on manufacturing alone isn't enough; innovation and unique designs must take precedence. The government is encouraged to monitor technology advancements, pushing for their commercialization.
item.dc:creator: CHETHAN KUMAR

item.title: Student killed, 17 injured as lighting frame collapses during dandiya event at Hyd college
item.description: A dandiya celebration at MVSR Engineering College led to a tragic incident on Saturday evening. A metal lighting frame collapsed during the festivities, resulting in one student's death and 17 others being injured. The Chief Minister expressed shock over the incident, directing police to take strict action against those responsible. Injured students were quickly helped and shifted to various hospitals for medical treatment.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Locked out, shut in, left hungry: Afghanistan after Taliban takeover
item.description: Since the Taliban's resurgence in Afghanistan, women's rights and access to education have suffered dramatically. Millions of girls are now prohibited from secondary and higher education, leading to dire social repercussions. In addition, food insecurity is rampant, affecting approximately 19.2 million individuals. The healthcare available has also significantly declined, obstructing women's ability to obtain necessary medical assistance. The overall humanitarian crisis continues to worsen, deeply affecting Afghan families' daily lives.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: 12 killed after speeding truck runs over devotees near temple in Gwalior
item.description: A tragic accident occurred in Gwalior where a truck lost control and hit devotees waiting by a temple. Thirteen individuals lost their lives in the incident that took place in the early hours of Sunday. Nearly 40 others sustained injuries, with several reported to be in serious condition. Police and rescue teams are working to assist the injured at the scene.
item.dc:creator: VIVEK DUBEY

item.title: 'India an important ally': Rubio explains why Trump paused sanctions on Russia oil buyers
item.description: The US government has opted to lift specific sanctions concerning the import of Russian oil and gas. This includes a review period of 60 days to evaluate the economic effects on key importers such as India and China. Senator Marco Rubio highlighted India's persistent dependency on Russian energy sources despite attempts to explore alternatives.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: 'You have to wait': Iyer explains why Sooryavanshi missed all 5 T20Is
item.description: India captain Shreyas Iyer urged Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to remain patient and trust his process despite missing the entire West Indies T20I series. Iyer praised consistent openers Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma. Reflecting on India's 2-2 series draw, he blamed inconsistent bowling for missed opportunities and praised West Indies captain Shai Hope, who won Player of the Series.

item.title: Major fire at Canadian military base in Alberta, Carney calls it ‘serious incident’
item.description: A major fire erupted at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta on Saturday, prompting concern among officials. Prime Minister Mark Carney deemed the situation serious, highlighting the safety of impacted personnel. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith labeled the blaze significant, emphasizing its repercussions for military staff. While the cause and damage details remain undisclosed, the federal government is actively collaborating with local agencies to manage the crisis.

item.description: Ajay Devgn's 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' saw a 61.3% increase in box office collections on its third Saturday. The movie earned Rs 5 crore on Day 16, improving its cumulative domestic net collection to Rs 341.10 crore. Its worldwide gross collection reached Rs 528.77 crore, with domestic and overseas contributions. The film, which continues the story from its predecessor, features an ensemble cast including Tabu and Shriya Saran.

Emergency services acted quickly, transporting the seriously injured to Calcutta Medical College.

item.description: The incident occurred around 7.40 pm in the Girish Park police station area amid heavy crowds of pandal visitors and rainfall. As rain began, people waiting outside the pandal rushed forward, causing some to fall on the road and triggering a stampede, a senior police officer told PTI. All the injured were rescued and taken to Calcutta Medical College for treatment.

item.description: A chaotic stampede unfolded at the Sarada Park Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata due to a crowd surge, leading to at least 1 deaths and 15 injuries. Emergency services transported the injured to Calcutta Medical College and Hospital for immediate medical assistance. The West Bengal health minister, alongside other political leaders, responded by visiting the scene and the hospital.

item.description: In a heartbreaking incident at a Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata, a stampede claimed the lives of at least 19 people and left 25 others injured amid a surge of visitors driven by panic from heavy rains. Rescue efforts were promptly initiated, and medical staff rushed the injured to hospitals.
